findings.caveat: PyBytesWriter is a different API SHAPE, not a rename: create/grow/finish instead of allocate-then-resize-in-place. Migration is per-buffer restructuring. Modules/_pickle.c:2783-2836 has already migrated one buffer to it, so the target idiom is demonstrated in the same file as the four remaining call sites.
findings.detail: _PyBytes_Resize is deprecated since 3.15. The named replacement is PyBytesWriter API, but it is NOT a drop-in. Modules/_pickle.c:2783-2836 has already migrated one buffer to it, so the target idiom is demonstrated in the same file as the four remaining call sites. (Doc/whatsnew/3.15.rst, Deprecated C APIs. 30 real call sites across Objects/ + Modules/.)

findings.caveat: PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr() is NOT a drop-in: it tests `type == &PyUnicode_Type` EXACTLY (Objects/unicode_writer.c:364), so a str subclass falls through to PyObject_Str(obj) and runs a user __str__ -- that was gh-148241, and Modules/_json.c:407 carries a comment saying so two lines above the call. The verified drop-in is PyUnicodeWriter_WriteSubstring(writer, str, 0, PyUnicode_GET_LENGTH(str)): it type-checks with PyUnicode_Check (Objects/unicode_writer.c:443, accepts subclasses) and tail-calls _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr for the full range (Objects/unicode_writer.c:412-414), so it is behaviour-identical for three integer comparisons.
findings.detail: _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr is deprecated since 3.14 and is scheduled for removal in 3.18. The named replacement is PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr, but it is NOT a drop-in. CAVEAT: PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr() is NOT a drop-in: it tests `type == &PyUnicode_Type` EXACTLY (Objects/unicode_writer.c:364), so a str subclass falls through to PyObject_Str(obj) and runs a user __str__ -- that was gh-148241, and Modules/_json.c:407 carries a comment saying so two lines above the call. The verified drop-in is PyUnicodeWriter_WriteSubstring(writer, str, 0, PyUnicode_GET_LENGTH(str)): it type-checks with PyUnicode_Check (Objects/unicode_writer.c:443, accepts subclasses) and tail-calls _PyUnicodeWriter_WriteStr for the full range (Objects/unicode_writer.c:412-414), so it is behaviour-identical for three integer comparisons. Marked _Py_DEPRECATED_EXTERNALLY, which expands to nothing under Py_BUILD_CORE -- CPython's own build emits no warning for this call, so it will not show up in a compiler log. (Include/cpython/unicodeobject.h:600.)
